articleTitle: The application of genetic algorithms to the optimal selection of parameter values in neural networks for attitude control systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on High Accuracy Platform Control in Space
abstract: Spacecraft attitude control is conventionally achieved by the use of reaction wheel or thruster based control schemes. The authors investigate the use of a neural network controller for a thruster based spacecraft attitude control system. They propose to train the neural network using a genetic algorithm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The vibration environment on a satellite in orbit
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on High Accuracy Platform Control in Space
abstract: Platform vibration is likely to become one of the problems affecting the design of high pointing accuracy payloads of future spacecraft. There are two aspects to this issue: (1) the vibration of the spacecraft transmitted to the payload requires development of an appropriate pointing control strategy to reduce the effects of this vibration, and (2) the vibration produced by the payload itself needs to be limited so that other vibration sensitive systems attached to the spacecraft are not adversely affected. One may thus think of a payload as either a recipient or as a source of vibration. The authors review the experience of the in-orbit environment of the Olympus telecommunications satellite and discuss the nature of the vibration produced by a variety of devices by reference to measurements from the spacecraft.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Rapid prototyping for real-time systems design
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on High Accuracy Platform Control in Space
abstract: The use of rapid prototyping design methodologies for real time control systems development have become more accepted within production engineering organizations. The author uses a case study of the Multiple Sensor Technology Integration (MSTI) program to consider some of the problems with traditional design approaches and attempts to quantify some advantages of rapid prototyping. The development of the operational real-time flight software for the MSTI spacecraft using rapid prototyping techniques is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of statistical techniques in the analysis of spacecraft pointing-an updated ESA error handbook
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on High Accuracy Platform Control in Space
abstract: Pointing and measurement specifications are generally formulated within a statistical framework, requiring compliance to be demonstrated using statistically justifiable techniques. The application of Bayesian MAP in the manner described appears to provide a justifiable method for the inclusion of measurement data (and errors) into the probability density function assignment of a component error. In particular, the method allows for the treatment of errors where data is sparse or not readily interpretable in the correct statistical fashion. These ideas, coupled with other modifications in the new error handbook, appear to provide a framework for the production of realistic, statistically justifiable and unambiguous spacecraft pointing performance estimates.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Nanotechnology in space: precision positioning and measuring using piezoelectric translators and capacitance micrometers
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on High Accuracy Platform Control in Space
abstract: Capacitance micrometers are ideal for measuring movements and deflections from millimetres down to picometres. They are compact, reliable and easy to fabricate onto a structure being monitored. Their linearity, are completely hysteresis free and have the advantage of zero power dissipation at the sensing position. Once a displacement has been measured, by whatever means, piezoelectric translators provide a very convenient method of correcting it. Piezoelectric translators can also be used to produce wanted displacements or rotations. The disadvantages of piezoelectrics such as nonlinearity, hysteresis and creep can be overcome by using them in a closed-loop configuration with capacitance micrometers or other position sensors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of neuro-Kalman filtering to attitude estimation of platforms and space vehicles
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on High Accuracy Platform Control in Space
abstract: In this paper the on going work concerning the application of a particular hybrid neural network and Kalman filtering approach to the attitude estimation problem is presented. A neural network architecture for implementing observers and estimators has been developed. A synergistic approach is adopted not only in learning the weights but also in the development of the macro structure of the neural network. Based on this architecture extended Kalman filtering and neural network learning are combined and implemented to the attitude estimation problem.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Model reduction methods for the analysis of control-structure interaction in flexible space structures
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on High Accuracy Platform Control in Space
abstract: Highlights some of the problems a design engineer encounters when reducing the order of a flexible space structure model. The choice of the appropriate method in a particular situation is dependant on characteristics of the model, the error criterion of importance and the end use of the model. Other methods of measuring errors in reduced order models are also studied. A realistic space vehicle mathematical model is currently being obtained and will be investigated using multiple inputs and outputs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Ion thrusters for orbit/attitude control of large flexible spacecraft
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on High Accuracy Platform Control in Space
abstract: Explores and identifies the issues involved in the application of ion thrusters (ITs) to the control of large flexible space structures. The performance and operational characteristics of ITs are outlined, including thrust throttling, startup response time and redundancy, and some aspects of application of ITs to control are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Simulated annealing applied to controlled design for large flexible space structures
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on High Accuracy Platform Control in Space
abstract: Summary form only given. Shows how simulated annealing can be applied to the controller placement problem for large scale linear time invariant systems under linear state feedback. Particular attention is paid to the four important-stages in the design of an algorithm based on this approach. Some initial results on the application of this approach to a large flexible space structure problems are presented together with some topics for short to medium term further research.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Flexible structure experiments at JPL and WPAFB: H/sub infinity / controller designs
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on High Accuracy Platform Control in Space
abstract: A number of control system experiments were carried out during 1990 and 1991 on two contrasting flexible space structure facilities. The first facility is the JPL/AFAL flexible antenna in Pasadena, California. The second is the WPAFB/AFWL 12-meter cantilever truss in Dayton, Ohio. Each structure possesses a number of flexible modes of vibration which are lightly damped. The purpose of the experiments was to achieve active damping of the flexible modes via a digital control system. The control system designs were carried out using an H/sub infinity /-based technique of 'weighted gap optimization', which is closely related to Glover-McFarlane loop-shaping.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Interpolating sliding mode control: an approach to high precision platform control with uncertain dynamics
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on High Accuracy Platform Control in Space
abstract: The robustness properties of sliding mode control are exploited in achieving high precision manoeuvring of a space platform to which are attached flexible appendages exhibiting an arbitrary number of flexure modes. Continuous control actuators are assumed. The dynamics parameters are assumed to be unknown but to lie within reasonable practical limits. A new continuous form of discrete-time sliding mode control law is employed. The effects of increasing the iteration interval of the onboard algorithm and errors in the assumed forward path DC gain on the precision with which the platform follows a controlled rate slew demand are investigated. The degree of active flexure mode damping is also investigated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
